title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 93-94
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 93 to 94 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'सत्त्ववान्सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 93 to 94 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 93 to 94.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 93 to 94** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **सत्त्ववान्सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**सत्त्ववान्सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः । अभिप्रायः प्रियार्होऽर्हः प्रियकृत्प्रीतिवर्धनः ॥** **विहायसगतिर्ज्योतिः सुरुचिर्हुतभुग्विभुः । रविर्विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रविलोचनः ॥**

Full of goodness, pure in nature, truth itself, rooted in the dharma of truth is he. The purpose of all and the one worthy of the beloved is that God of gods. Worthy of worship, the doer of what is dear, who makes love grow. He travels the sky, the light, the lovely glow, the fire that eats the offerings. The Sun, the shining one, Savita, with the Sun as his eye, is that God of gods.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 93 to 94 mean?
faq.a: Full of goodness, pure in nature, truth itself, rooted in the dharma of truth is he. The purpose of all and the one worthy of the beloved is that God of gods. Worthy of worship, the doer of what is dear, who makes love grow. He travels the sky, the light, the lovely glow, the fire that eats the offerings. The Sun, the shining one, Savita, with the Sun as his eye, is that God of gods.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
